title: Threaded comments
description: Threaded comments for any resource in a multi-tenant app: post and reply with a depth limit, @mentions, edit window, soft delete, paginated lists with reply previews, emoji reactions, user flags with auto-hide and moderation, with injected authorization, a PostgreSQL store and a Fetch adapter.

notes: Requires a TypeScript build, crypto.randomUUID, TextEncoder/TextDecoder, btoa/atob and the Fetch Request/Response APIs: Node.js 22+, Bun, Deno, Cloudflare Workers, Next.js route handlers and Hono.
Framework-neutral core; mount the HTTP adapter with your framework's catch-all route.
No runtime packages, environment reads, timers or network activity at install or import time.

configuration: On PostgreSQL, apply schema.sql and use createSqlCommentStore with your query executor; on other databases implement CommentStore with primary keys on (comment_id, user_id, emoji) and (comment_id, user_id) and an atomic flag counter.
Implement authorize(actor, action, {tenantId, resourceType, resourceId}) for read, post and moderate from your own membership and resource-access checks.
Implement authenticate(request) from your session or verified token, never from the request body.
Tune editWindowMs, maxDepth, maxBodyLength, flagThreshold, previewReplies and the reactions allow-list; pass sanitize only if you store rich text.
Resolve mentions to users and send notifications in your own code after post or edit; the module only extracts the handles.
Mount createCommentHandler under one prefix with exact allowedOrigins; it complements, not replaces, your CSRF policy.
limitations: Does not resolve @mentions to accounts, send notifications, render HTML or sanitize rich text; it stores plain text unless you pass sanitize.
No moderation queue listing, edit history or realtime delivery; build those on the store (schema.sql has a hidden-comments index).
The in-memory store is for tests and prototypes only; the SQL store is tested on PostgreSQL semantics through PGlite, which runs one connection, not on every hosted Postgres under parallel load.
No rate limiting; add request rate limits (see the rate-limit module) on post, reaction and flag routes.
Production database correctness, session security, content policy and consuming-application acceptance remain project responsibilities.

verification.command: npm run build && node --test tests/comments.test.mjs tests/comments-sql.test.mjs
behaviors: replies nest to maxDepth; a deeper reply fails with too-deep
a parent on another resource, another tenant, unknown or deleted fails with invalid-parent
@mentions are extracted and deduplicated, and email addresses are not mentions
the author edits within the edit window; afterwards only a moderator may edit, and editedAt is kept
soft delete clears the body and mentions, keeps replies, and the thread still lists them
top-level comments list newest first with an opaque cursor; replies preview oldest first with replyCount
reactions toggle per user and emoji, report the actor's own, and refuse emoji outside the allow-list
each user flags once; a visible comment is hidden at the threshold, approved comments are not auto-hidden, and moderators approve or hide
ids from another tenant are not-found, and read-only or outside users are forbidden to post, react or moderate
HTTP adapter: every route, status codes, origin check, 401 when signed out and cache-control no-store
schema.sql applies and the SQL store passes the core behaviors on PostgreSQL
50 concurrent reactions from 25 users and 10 concurrent removals end with exact counts
24 concurrent flags from 12 users record exactly 12 and hide exactly at the threshold

changes: First release: core, in-memory store, PostgreSQL schema and store, and Fetch adapter.
